name: Internet & New-Age Tech

mofsl_2qfy27.headline: No dedicated Internet & New-Age Tech section in the 2QFY27 compendium (page 13 onward runs Automobiles to Utilities with no Internet page)
mofsl_2qfy27.read: MOFSL covers 13 Internet & New-Age Tech companies but prints no sector narrative or guidance. Its sector PAT charts show Internet as the top gainer in 1HFY27 (loss-to-profit), with Internet also leading 2HFY27E PAT growth (loss-to-profit), and the FY28E earnings-revision table names Internet & New-Age Tech, with Technology and Telecom, as sectors that weighed on the 0.7% FY28 upgrade to the MOFSL Universe. Eternal appears among the stocks driving index-level earnings. Company-level numbers must come from company decks and broker notes, not this report.

unit_economics: Platform: NOV (net order value) = orders x NAOV; adjusted revenue = NOV x take rate (commission + ads + fees); contribution = revenue - delivery cost - discounts - other variable; Adj EBITDA = contribution - fixed cost - rent. Quick commerce adds stores x NOV per store per day and gross profit under inventory model. Payments: GMV x net take in bp + devices x rent. Travel and marketplaces: GMV x take rate.

price_drivers.driver: Quick commerce contribution margin and competitive discounting
price_drivers.why: Funded entrants decide whether Instamart-type losses (about -1.4% of NOV in Q2FY27) narrow; basket-discount gaps lead contribution by about a quarter.

price_drivers.driver: Food delivery NOV growth and take rate
price_drivers.why: FD growth near 20% with adjusted take ~30-34% of NOV funds the group; zero-commission entrants and platform-fee limits cap take.

price_drivers.driver: Adjusted EBITDA after rent and ESOP
price_drivers.why: ESOP was ~69% of Eternal's FY26 Adj EBITDA, so core EBITDA after ESOP is the number valued, not segment results.
Capex of INR2.5-3.6 cr per store and 12-14 days NWC under inventory model set whether store adds earn their cost of capital.

price_drivers.driver: Regulation: gig-worker levies, UPI MDR, FDI rules
price_drivers.why: Social-security levy of 1-2% of turnover (capped at 5% of payouts), UPI MDR framework and IOCC rules change unit economics by rule.

kpis.name: GOV / NOV / GMV growth with orders x order value split
kpis.definition: Gross or net order value growth by segment, split into users, frequency and order value, on a like-for-like perimeter.
kpis.formula: Orders x NAOV; GOV x NOV/GOV
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Growth earned through MTU and frequency is rewarded; discount-funded GOV is not (Eternal FD GOV ran 4pp ahead of NOV in Q2FY26), and share moves when two companies' growth gap exceeds ~4pp.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'GOV' / 'NOV' / 'GMV' / 'orders' / 'MTU' (ETERNAL, SWIGGY, PAYTM, PINELABS, IXIGO, NYKAA); get_financials for revenue; shareholder letters in the library.
kpis.estimate_source: get_consensus_estimates gives Bloomberg Sales for the group; GOV/NOV forecasts come from broker models in the report library.
kpis.traps: Eternal sunset GOV for NOV from Q1FY27; Swiggy reports margins on GOV; perimeter changes (Bistro, Toing, Paytm ticketing); MOFSL has no sector table.

kpis.name: Take rate (adjusted revenue or gross profit % of NOV)
kpis.definition: Adjusted revenue (commission + ads + customer fees) over NOV for marketplaces; gross profit % NOV under inventory model; net payment revenue in bp of GMV for payments.
kpis.formula: Adjusted revenue / NOV; GP / NOV; NPR / GMV
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Platform-fee rises (Rs2 to Rs13) drove margin for three years; each Rs1 is ~26bp of NOV, so a cap or a zero-commission rival cuts the take that funds the margin.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'take rate' / 'adjusted revenue' / 'net payment revenue' / 'PPM'; get_financials for revenue; transcripts for fee changes.
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus field; Broker models in the report library; company commentary.
kpis.traps: 1P transition grosses up revenue (Blinkit from Q2FY26); gross vs net payments revenue (Paytm gross, Pine Labs net); take on NOV vs GOV vs revenue differs by broker.

kpis.name: Contribution margin per order (% of NOV, Rs per order)
kpis.definition: Revenue less delivery cost, platform-funded discounts and other variable cost, with scope (rent in or out) stated.
kpis.formula: (Adjusted revenue - delivery - discounts - variable cost) / NOV
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Instamart contribution moved from -0.2% to -1.0% of GOV (-1.4% of NOV) in Q2FY27 as competitors matched discounts; contribution sets how fast a challenger converges to breakeven.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'contribution' (ETERNAL, SWIGGY); shareholder letters; transcripts.
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus field; Company guidance (Swiggy Instamart 0 to -100bp) and broker models.
kpis.traps: Eternal and Swiggy define scope differently; GOV vs NOV base changes the magnitude 35-45%; rent above or below the line.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA and core EBITDA after ESOP
kpis.definition: Company Adj EBITDA (post-rent, pre-ESOP, ex other income) and house core EBITDA after recurring ESOP, by segment.
kpis.formula: Segment result - rent; Adj EBITDA - recurring ESOP
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Group profit is the sum of FD profits less QC and new-bet losses; Eternal FY26 Adj EBITDA was INR1,189 cr but core EBITDA after INR819 cr ESOP only ~INR370 cr.
kpis.history_source: get_financials (segment results, ESOP, lease note); get_investor_presentation metric filter 'Adjusted EBITDA'; shareholder letters.
kpis.estimate_source: get_consensus_estimates Bloomberg EBITDA / PAT / EPS (bases mixed: pre- and post-ESOP); broker models give segment EBITDA.
kpis.traps: Segment result excludes rent; treasury and tax drive PAT (Eternal ETR 61-66%); street bases mix pre-ESOP EBITDA with different share counts.

kpis.name: Dark stores, NOV per store per day and capex per store
kpis.definition: Store count, net adds, NOV (or orders) per store per day on average stores, capex per net add and NWC days.
kpis.formula: Quick commerce NOV / average stores / days
kpis.unit: Rs lakh per store per day, Rs cr per store
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Store adds into served pincodes dilute throughput; breakeven needs ~Rs7 lakh GOV per day (about 800-1,000 orders) and company frameworks assume Rs2.5 cr capex and 12 days NWC.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'stores' / 'NOV per store' / 'orders per store'; Sensor Tower and locator data cited in broker notes in the library.
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus field; Store-count guidance in transcripts (Eternal's store target; Swiggy CMD framework) and broker models.
kpis.traps: Period-end vs average stores; Swiggy restated orders per store per day (active-store-days); frameworks are not delivered results.

kpis.name: MTU and order frequency
kpis.definition: Monthly transacting users and orders per user per month.
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Frequency fell 23% YoY at Instamart when AOV was engineered up; users and frequency show whether growth is share gain or price.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'MTU' / 'frequency' (ETERNAL, SWIGGY, IXIGO, NYKAA); app-trend data in broker notes (Sensor Tower via CLSA).
kpis.traps: Eternal MTU definitions include merchant-app users at Paytm; Sensor Tower restated history in Sep-26.

kpis.name: Net payment revenue in bp of GMV and MDR status
kpis.definition: Payments revenue after processing charges, excluding incentives, per unit of merchant GMV.
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Paytm NPR ex-PIDF ran ~8.4-9bp of GMV; UPI MDR framework (0.40% above Rs2,000, go-live pending) is the swing factor brokers value at Rs470-1,200 cr for FY28.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'net payment revenue' / 'GMV' / 'PPM' (PAYTM, PINELABS); get_financials; transcripts.
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus field; Bloomberg Sales/EBITDA/PAT/EPS only; MDR sizing from broker notes.
kpis.traps: Gross vs net reporting; PIDF and UPI incentives inside other operating revenue; DLG expense timing in lending.

kpis.name: Gross bookings and take rate (online travel)
kpis.definition: Gross booking value and revenue as % of GBV for online travel agencies.
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Bookings growth with stable take and falling marketing share drives operating leverage at asset-light travel platforms.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'GBV' / 'gross bookings' / 'air tickets' (IXIGO); get_financials.
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus field; Bloomberg Sales/EBITDA only for IXIGO.
kpis.traps: Gross vs net revenue recognition; one-off ad and convenience-fee changes.

valuation_anchor: SOTP by segment: food delivery EV/core EBITDA (street 30-40x forward Adj EBITDA, re-base for ESOP), quick commerce EV/NOV with implied steady-state margin plus DCF, challenger on DCF with losses to breakeven; payments on core NPR DCF plus separate MDR NPV and treasury.
watch_next_quarter: MOFSL has no Internet guidance section; from its charts, Internet is the largest 2HFY27E PAT-growth contributor (loss-to-profit) and its Retail page flags festive demand shifting into 3QFY27, so track festive-quarter NOV, quick-commerce discounting against funded entrants, store additions and Paytm's MDR go-live.
